**Surah 74: al-Muddaththir**

Its purpose is earnest striving and diligence in warning the arrogant of the abode of ruin, and establishing the resurrection in the souls of the deniers, the wicked. It also points to good tidings for the people of remembrance, through the forbearance of the Mighty, the Forgiving. Its name, al-Muddaththir, is the clearest indication of this, as is evident to whoever reflects on the address, the one addressed, and the cause. (In the name of God), the King, the Most High, the One, the Subduer, (the Compassionate), who encompasses all with the two blessings of existence and clear expression, for the righteous and the wicked alike, (the Merciful), who singles out the people of His chosen ones with insight and with success in reaching the abode of permanence.

* *

When al-Muzzammil was concluded with good tidings for the people of insight, after it had begun with striving in the service that prepares one to bear the burdens of the call, this surah opens [with the point of departure -] the wisdom of the message, which is warning the people of loss. He says, expressing with what contains good tidings of abundance in wealth, men, righteousness and good condition in the present and the future, and making known that the one addressed is in the utmost state of alertness of heart, even if (p-40) he has covered his outward form: ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾, one who has wrapped himself in his garment, meaning he has enveloped himself with it. The *dithar* (with a kasra) is what lies over the *shi'ar* among garments, and the *shi'ar* is what clings to the body. "The Helpers are the *shi'ar*, and the people are the *dithar*." *Dthur* means the many passersby; *dathara* of a tree means its leaves; and *tadthir* of a bird means its tending to its nest. The expression with the particle suitable for both nearness and distance is intended to convey utmost nearness, by what the context indicates, even though the expression with this particle contains a kind of concealment, fitting for one who is wrapped. It was chosen because nothing is said after it of what is greater and more majestic. The *dithar* had not covered his noble body entirely, as indicated by the expression with *idgham* rather than *izhar*. The *izhar* would indicate intensity. The purpose was only to cover the eye so that the heart would be gathered; covering the head and what is near it of the body suffices for this. The *idgham* (here, the assimilation of the two identical letters, *al-muddaththir* rather than *al-mutadaththir* being read with the doubled letter) is highly suitable to the *dithar*.

When he was in the state of wrapping himself up, he had kept to one place, and so his noble self was kept hidden. Therefore he was commanded (ﷺ) to stand, and warning was made a consequence of this, indicating that what is intended for him, that he would become the most widely known of creation through the general message, requires hitching up the garment and driving himself with the utmost earnestness and striving, which is the necessary result of the great spread of his message. So it is contrary to wrapping oneself up in every respect. He said: ﴿Arise﴾, meaning any kind of standing, especially from the place of your wrapping, with the utmost resolve and earnestness.

When the matter at the beginning of the revelation of this surah was that people had been overtaken by corruption, one of the describers of the message mentioned it, signalling the great need for him. So he said, as a consequence of his standing: ﴿And warn﴾, meaning, carry out warning for everyone who can be warned. He warned whoever was lying asleep in his heedlessness, wrapped in the garments of his intoxication, neglectful of what lies before him of the terrors of the Day of Resurrection. Likewise, he warned whoever was awake but wrapped in the garments of his confusions and the coverings of his lapses. Every creature is obliged to thank its Lord, or else He will punish him, either for his obstinacy toward Him or for his heedlessness of Him, by whatever is least of turning away from Him. He omitted the object to indicate that the warning is general to everyone who could possibly oppose it by reason, and they are all of creation. That is because (ﷺ) Gabriel, peace be upon him, had come down to him with ﴿Read in the name of your Lord﴾ [al-'Alaq: 1] and similar verses, and by that he became a prophet. Then this verse came down to him, and by it he became a messenger. This happened when he was called while he was on Mount Hira. When he heard the voice, he looked right and left and saw nothing. Then he raised his head, and there was Gabriel, peace be upon him, sitting on a throne between heaven and earth. He was seized with the utmost fear, and he hurried to come to the house, his shoulders trembling, and he said:

"Wrap me up, wrap me up! Indeed I have feared for myself. Pour cold water over me."

When warning (*indhar*) involves confronting people with what they dislike, and that is grave for a human being, and the one who holds back from following the caller (*da'i*) has one of two matters: leaving what he is commanded to do, or seeking a wage from him in return, just as what compels following him is his acting upon what he calls to and his distance from taking a wage for it, He commanded him to magnify (*ta'zim*) the One who sent him, glory be to Him. For when one magnifies Him with the magnification due to Him, everything beneath Him becomes small, so calling becomes easy for him, and He becomes a helper to him in being accepted. So He said: ﴿And your Lord﴾, i.e., the One who nurtures you specifically, ﴿so magnify﴾, i.e., arise. Thus, from your rising with utmost earnestness and striving, you describe Him alone with greatness, in speech and in belief, in every state. That is to declare Him free of association (*shirk*) first of all things, and likewise free of everything that does not befit Him, of joining and separating, of asking other than Him, and of being occupied with other than Him.

Imam Abu Ja'far Ibn al-Zubayr said: Its fitting with Surat al-Muzzammil is clear. The opening of the two surahs is of one pattern, and what each of them begins with, from His sublime address to him, peace be upon him, and His great honoring: ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 1], ﴿O you who are wrapped in a cloak﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 1]. The command in both is with what is specific to him: ﴿Stand [in prayer] by night, except a little﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 2], ﴿half of it﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 3], and so on; and in the other, ﴿Arise and warn﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 2] (p-43) ﴿and your Lord, so magnify﴾. In the first, it was followed by His saying: ﴿And be patient over what they say﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 10]; and in the second, by His saying ﴿And for your Lord, be patient﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 7]. All of that is one purpose. In al-Muzzammil, the command to patience was followed by threatening and warning the disbelievers: ﴿And leave Me with the deniers﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 11], and so on; and likewise in the other: ﴿Leave Me with whom I created alone﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 11], and so on. So the two surahs come in one context and a single unified purpose. End of quotation.

Since purifying the servant from defilements is for the sake of purifying the One worshipped, He said, commanding the purification of the outward and the inward by perfecting the theoretical faculty in magnifying Him, glorified is He, so that he may be fit to be among the people of His presence—and this is the first command given to one who abandons blameworthy customs: ﴿And your garments, purify﴾, meaning: arise and single out your sensory garments by keeping them away from impurities, by avoiding the habits of the arrogant in lengthening them, and by purifying them so that they are fit to stand in service in the holy and spiritual presence. The spiritual (ma'nawiyyah) garments are everything that encompasses the servant of blameworthy morals and sickly habits: slackness in service, weariness, and indulgence in some of the habits of the self. This is made easy by perfecting the theoretical faculty.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 74, verse 5:

When He commanded to keep away from the soiling of garments, and intended both the sensory and the non-sensory (meanings), and that was apparent in the sensory sense, and He made that a metaphor (kinayah) for avoiding all filth, because whoever keeps his clothing free of it has, by a fortiori reasoning (min bab al-awla), kept it far from himself, (p-44) he established the generality and emphasized it, saying: ﴿And uncleanness﴾, that is, every kind of filth, for it is the cause of the lowly deeds which are the cause of punishment. In al-Qamus it says: ar-rijz, with a kasra or a damma: filth, the worship of idols, punishment, and polytheism.

﴿So forsake﴾, that is, keep away openly and in worship, so that you may obtain the reward just as you used to keep away from it secretly and by habit, and so you obtained the good praise, to the extent that the Quraysh used to call you "the Trustworthy" (al-Amin) and would not dispute with you over anything.

Having begun with one of the two causes of acceptance, he follows it with the second, which keeps far from the breaker of deeds: self-admiration, showing off, and weariness. So he says: ﴿And do not bestow favor﴾ [i.e.,] upon anyone by your supplication for him, or by something you give him as a gift or a loan, by making the pleasure of the one you have done good to bitter through burdening him with your mention of it in a manner of superiority and magnifying what you have done with him. Or [it means]: do not give anything while you are ﴿seeking more﴾, i.e., seeking to give back a reward or more than what you have given. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, and it comes from the expression "man—" when he gives. That is because it is the most fitting for the giver among creatures that he regard what he gives as little and thank Allah who enabled him to give it, and for the receiver that he regard what he has received as much. So the Prophet ﷺ was commanded not to do anything for any cause at all, but purely for Allah. For when the desire for more is removed, sincerity is attained, since his aim is not attached to seeking a equivalent, let alone seeking a return. Thus the deed reaches the utmost purity: it is not intended for any reward at all, nor is it desired for other than the Face of Allah, the Exalted. This is the ultimate in sincerity.

(p-45) Since warning is so hard on the souls that it brings about treatments of such a kind that death is lighter than them, because abandoning what is familiar is the hardest thing for souls, and so is abandoning benefits, He said, commanding adornment with the Protector (al-'Asim) after emptying oneself of the Breaker (al-Qasim), informing that harm from those who warn is something unavoidable, so that one enters obedience with insight. The situation therefore requires that warning becomes easier through independence from the perishing ones and through being with the Enduring One alone. He indicated this by putting the Deity first, describing Him by the attribute of Benevolence as an encouragement, and said: ﴿And for your Lord﴾, that is, the One who is beneficent to you, who nurtures you, who alone manages all your interests, ﴿so be patient﴾ [that is -] over the hardships of the obligations, in commands and prohibitions, over the harm of the polytheists, over the rigor of life and all afflictions, for He will abundantly reward you with the good of both abodes, in such a way that He does not make you need anyone, and makes people need you, and eases for you the bearing of hardships in both abodes, especially the matter of the Day of Resurrection, for whoever bears the work in this world, the work will bear him in the Hereafter.

(p-46) Since the context calls for warning, and whoever rejects the commands by denying them has disbelieved, and whoever neglects them has neither obeyed nor given thanks, he cautioned against slackness in regard to them by mentioning what awaits the one who denies them. So he said, as a consequence of that, urging the earning of good deeds without laziness or hesitation, reminding that the King has put the horn to his mouth and bent his forehead to it, waiting for the command to blow, and by using the passive form he indicated its humiliation before Him and its lightness for Him, and by the particle of certainty he indicated that it must certainly occur: ﴿So when the trumpet is sounded﴾, that is, when it is blown and sounds with intensity, force, penetration and impact, ﴿into the Naqur﴾, that is, the Sur (trumpet), which is the horn that Israfil (peace be upon him) is now holding to his mouth, bent in waiting for the command to blow into it for the Resurrection. It may also be that what is meant is the days in which the disbelievers are humbled, such as the Day of Badr, the Conquest and others, just as the Hour and the Resurrection have been made a metaphor for death. So the Prophet (ﷺ) said:

"Whoever dies, his resurrection has come." He expressed it with the word "naqr" (striking), indicating that in its severity it is like striking on a hard surface, so that a terrifying sound results from it. The root of "naqr" is knocking, which is the cause of sound, so it is more severe than one who warns them for the sake of caution against the abode of destruction. Then the spirits will be returned to their bodies, and people will be raised and will stand up from their graves as a single soul, and you will see the outcome of patience, and your enemies will see the outcome of arrogance. The expression here uses the intensive form and makes it the doer, like a spy, indicating increased greatness, until it is as if it is itself the one acting, in a form of utmost severity and strength. The Prophet (ﷺ) cautioned his companions (may Allah be pleased with them) about blowing into the trumpets and its nearness, and they said: "How should we say it, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Say: Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs." It may also be that the consequence is of the command to patience, meaning: be patient, for We shall surely take vengeance for you on that day in a way that will comfort your eye, so this is consolation for him (ﷺ) and a threat to them.

When he had mentioned this condition, "is it (?)" that he depicted [with its -] terrifying forms, he answered it with his saying: ﴿So that﴾, i.e., that time, the hard, severe, extremely intense time, reaching in its hardship a degree to which one points with a pointing like [that of what is -] the farthest of the far, and it is the time of the trumpet blast (al-naqr). Then he substituted for this mubtada' (the grammatical subject of the nominal sentence) another phrase, for added awe, his saying: ﴿on that Day﴾, i.e., the time when the terrifying trumpet blast will occur, ﴿is a difficult day﴾, i.e., one of extreme hardship.

﴿Upon the disbelievers﴾, that is, those who used to scorn the warning and turn away from it, because they are firmly rooted in disbelief, which is the concealing of what must be made manifest of the proofs of God's oneness. Since hardship (ʿusr) may be applied to a thing [و - ] in which there is ease from some aspects, or which, when treated, becomes easy, he clarified that it is not so by saying: ﴿not easy﴾. Thus he combined in it the affirmation of the thing and the negation of its opposite, to confirm its matter, to repel metaphor from it, to emphasize its existence, and because it is not cut off in any way. Restricting it to the disbelievers indicates that it is made easy for the believers.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 74, verse 11:

When this indicated that most of creation would meet the Day of Resurrection in their disbelief, their corrupt inner intention and their wicked affairs, and that this was something that would grieve him (ﷺ) out of his compassion for creation, and [since] He knew who had set themselves up for enmity against him, He made their affair easy for him and belittled their standing in His sight by His promise of sufficiency, through His saying, beginning a new statement, alerting to the causes of destruction, the greatest of which is delusion, which is the doubt of [his] wife, and [her] desire: ﴿Leave Me﴾, i.e., leave Me to deal [with him] in whatever state it happens; ﴿and whom﴾, i.e., together with everyone whom ﴿I created﴾, i.e., brought into being from non-existence and produced through the stages of creation, while he was ﴿alone﴾, having neither wealth, nor children, nor anything; and while I am One, firmly steadfast in the attribute of oneness, with no one sharing in My making of him. Yet he did not give thanks for this blessing, but rather disbelieved in it by associating partners with God, glorified is He, who is able to annihilate him after bringing him into being.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 74, verse 12:

Since what makes a person tyrannical (al-mutgha lil-insan) is the power (al-makna) whose circle is centred on wealth (al-mal), He said: ﴿And I made for him﴾ [i.e.,] with means that I brought into being by Myself alone, there being no power or strength from him, as evidenced by the fact that others are stronger than him in body and heart, and wider in thought and intellect, while he is inferior to them in that, ﴿wealth extended﴾, i.e., spread out, vast, growing, [very abundant,] comprehensive for all the times of his existence. What is meant by it, as will come, is al-Walid ibn al-Mughira. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: He had camels, and cultivated lands, and cattle, and gardens, and male and female slaves between Makkah and al-Ta'if.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 74, verse 13:

(p-49)[Since the first thing the soul reaches out to after abundance of wealth is children, and the dearest of children are males -] He said: ﴿and sons﴾. Since the need to be parted from them, even for a short time, is burdensome, and since their being most attached to him and most free from having to travel in the land was another blessing, He said: ﴿attending﴾, that is, present with him, because of his independence from journeys through abundance of wealth and the spread of servants [and] the strength of helpers. Even while present, they are at the peak of presence, with complete reason and strong sharpness, so they are in the utmost knowledge of whatever the awareness they gain allows; wherever he wants them he finds them, and he enjoys meeting them. Despite this, they are the notables of gatherings and the foremost of assemblies, as if no one else were witnessing them, among them Khalid, whom Allah blessed with Islam, so he became the Sword of Allah the Exalted and the Sword of His Messenger (ﷺ).

Since this [phrase] is a metaphor for abundance of provision and greatness of station, and whoever is granted wealth, children and standing has a soul that yearns for the completion of all that through preservation and facilitation, He said, appealing (to him) since it was so, by reminding him of His blessings: ﴿And I made smooth﴾, that is, gradually and thoroughly, ﴿for him﴾, that is, I prepared, spread out and readied (things) for him in leadership, by gathering for him, in addition to ownership of material things, ownership of the meanings through which hearts are (won), and I lengthened his life, removed from him the obstacles to comfortable living, and provided him with the means of high standing, until people submitted to him for this reason, and he dwelt in his land at ease, with the elders returning to his opinion. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him both, said: (p-50) "I extended for him what lies between Yemen and Syria, and I completed for him the happiness of this world, which necessitated his being unique in his time among his household and clan, to the extent that he was called 'the Unique' and 'the Fragrant Herb of Quraysh'. Yet he did not give thanks for this great blessing." [And] He emphasized that with His saying: ﴿(as) a making smooth﴾.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 74, verse 15:

When He, glorified is He, had done that for him, and this blessing led him to arrogance and haughtiness toward the One who had granted it to him, in contrast to what he should have had of gratitude and restraint, He said, affirming that it is He, glorified is He, who bestowed it upon him, and He is the One, the Subduer, indicating with the particle of delay (thumma) the improbability of any increase for him in his present state of ingratitude: ﴿Then﴾, meaning after the tremendous matter he committed of denying Our Messenger ﷺ, ﴿he aspires﴾, meaning without any cause he can present to Us from what We made a cause of increase in gratitude, ﴿that I should increase [him]﴾, meaning in what We have given him of his worldly life or his Hereafter, while he denies My Messenger ﷺ.

Since the implied meaning was: "Indeed he hopes for that, because wealth and standing bring nobility and greatness with the least effort. This is what is well known, commonly practiced and familiar," He (Glorified is He) began to rebuke him for that with the most comprehensive rebuke, as a sign among the signs of prophethood and a decisive proof of the truth of the message. He said what no one other than Him could say, since, while it contains no doubt or fabrication, it corresponds to reality. He [the man] did not increase after that at all, but remained in decline until he perished, and "the word of your Lord is fulfilled in truth and justice; none can alter His words" (6:115). ﴿Kalla﴾ ("No!"), meaning: by Our might and Our majesty, there will be no increase for him at all. As for decline, he will see it if he persists in denying. So let him refrain from this hope, let him be restrained and let him turn back, for it is sheer foolishness, pure adornment and utter delusion. When He had rebuked him with this rebuke, which must necessarily bring acceptance and true faith from one whom deprivation has not overcome, He gave the reason for it, emphasizing it against their obstinacy and their denial of the Return, saying: ﴿Indeed he﴾, that is, this described person, ﴿was﴾ by a disposition that seemed to be his innate nature and temperament, from which he cannot free himself, ﴿hostile to Our signs﴾, in respect of their great greatness specifically, because they guide to the Oneness [of God], and not to other doubts that lead to association [of partners with God], ﴿obstinate﴾, that is, extremely stubborn, to such a degree that his obstinacy toward them is not matched by his obstinacy toward anything else, owing to the extreme ugliness of his stubbornness. And ʿinād (stubborn obstinacy), as al-Malawi said, is one who is arrogant within himself, or dry in temperament, or harsh in character, or deranged in intellect. All of these were combined in Iblis, for he was created from fire, and fire by its nature is dryness and unwillingness to yield. Its reality is a deviation from the right path and an overstepping of bounds, together with persistence and adherence to it. From it comes opposing the truth while knowing that it is the truth.

[p. 51]

Since this (the matter just mentioned) stirs the desire to hear an explanation of this rebuke, and since obstinacy is a harshness of disposition and a sourness of character that brings about distress and hardship, He made its recompense of the same kind, and said: ﴿I will overwhelm him﴾ (sa'urhiquhu), meaning: I will bring him down with violence, harshness and subjugation, a bringing-down that overtakes him and surrounds him, with a threat that will not be broken. ﴿With a arduous ascent﴾ (sa'udan), meaning: something of calamities and distresses, as if it were an ascent (ʿaqabah). For ṣu'ūd, linguistically, is an ʿaqabah (steep climb) whose ascent is extremely difficult. At-Tirmidhi related from Abu Sa'id, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that it is a mountain of fire in which he climbs for seventy autumns and then falls down again. In another narration: whenever he puts his hand to the effort of ascending, it melts, and when he lifts it, it returns; and likewise his foot. Al-Kalbi said: it is a smooth rock in the Fire, which he is required to climb while being pulled from in front by chains of iron and struck from behind with iron maces; he climbs it for forty [years], and when he reaches its summit he is thrown down to its base, then he is required to climb it again, and so it is his perpetual lot.

Al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on Surah 74, verse 18:

When there arose a longing to know some of what he (al-Walid ibn al-Mughira) had used to oppose the verses, he said, explaining that and emphasizing the astonishment of the intelligent at what he did, because of how far it was from the right and because every person of sound intellect knows that it is a lie: ﴿Indeed he﴾, that is, this stubborn one, ﴿thought﴾, that is, he turned his thought over and around, following his own desire, in order to arrive at something with which to attack the Qur'an, ﴿and planned﴾, that is, he made a deliberate arrangement of the matters with which he would attack it, and preserved them (p-53) within himself, so that he might know which of them is closest to being accepted.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 74, verse 19:

When his scheming and calculating had caused others to perish by preventing them from the life of faith, he himself was struck by that which prevented him from a beneficial life in both abodes, and that is the perpetual perdition. Since the harm is only the perdition itself and not its being from a specific source, he expressed this in the passive form, saying, reporting and invoking a response that is granted and cannot fail to come to pass: ﴿Then he was killed﴾, meaning he perished, was cursed and was expelled in this his worldly life.

Since calculation is the ultimate of thinking, and thinking ought to guide him to what is right, but it led him to error, he marvelled at him and said, rebuking him and using the interrogative particle to indicate that this is something to be marvelled at and asked about: ﴿How did he calculate?﴾, meaning, in what manner did he bring about this calculation? And if the very notion of "manner" is denied, because it is hardly realized given its falsehood, then denying the particular kind of manner is even more fitting.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (*Nazm al-Durar*) on surah 74, verse 20:

Since his falling into this slander was extremely grave [due to the manifest lie it contains, and his opposition to the One who is the Mighty, the Firm, the Avenger, the Subduer, the Great], and due to other aspects that keep one far from falling into it, he emphasized the meaning as a deterrent against the like of it and as an incitement to repent from it. He said, using the particle of distance to indicate the greatness of this killing, both by the use of that particle and by repetition: ﴿Then he was killed﴾, meaning: this obstinate one perished and was cursed, a perishing and a cursing that are at the utmost greatness after death, in the barzakh (the intermediate state between death and resurrection) and on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿how he calculated﴾.

"When the skilled one in reasoning thinks and sets his thinking right, he examines its implications." He said, pointing to the length of his deliberation: ﴿Then he looked﴾, meaning: concerning what the matter of the Qur'an might be repelled with, time after time. In this is an indication of the ugliness of his actions, for the truth becoming manifest to him while he persists in obstinacy: repeated examination of the truth only increases it in clarity in every state, whereas with falsehood it increases nothing but weakness and lassitude.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 74, verse 22:

When the one who did so (i.e., who acted in this manner) became manifest in the corruption of his opinion, and stood by the portion of his own soul, he began to frown and to do things by which his form changed without his choosing, Allah said: ﴿Then he frowned﴾, meaning his face contracted and became sour and dour, so his face darkened, with the skin between the two eyes drawn tight out of intense aversion, like one who is accused and who thinks deeply about a matter for which he finds no way out, because the stratagems were closed to him, given that he found in what the Prophet (ﷺ) brought no point to attack. ﴿And he scowled﴾: "basara" is a follower (taukid) of "'abasa" to emphasize it. It may also convey that he examined what he had said and weighed it on the scale of thought, pursuing it excessively until his foot became firmly fixed in it. Thus they said that it is a follower if it is meant as emphasis; otherwise it has come in isolation. In the Qamus: "basara" means he frowned; "basara al-hajah" means he sought it out of its time; "basara al-din" means he demanded it before its due time. So it is as if, when the thinking lengthened upon him, he began to hasten its attainment toward his aim. It is also said: "basara" means he began a thing, so it is as if, when he frowned, the idea of magic occurred to him, and he began to display what had come to his mind about the matter. Ibn Burjan said: "al-busur" is a condition in the face that indicates sorrow in the heart.

Since this consideration, in this manner, is the most praiseworthy thing for the one considering it when nothing in it can be turned into a criticism, and since its outward appearance is that it is for the pursuit of truth, persisting in falsehood alongside it is at the furthest extreme of distance. He said, indicating by it the praise and the failure to find any criticism, and expressing it with the particle of distance: ﴿Then﴾, i.e., after this great deliberation, ﴿he turned his back﴾ [i.e. -] on what his thinking had led him to of belief in the soundness of the thing considered and its exaltedness above faultfinding, so he deviated from the faces of ideas to their backs. ﴿And he was arrogant﴾, i.e. [and -] he produced arrogance against acknowledging the truth, in the manner of one who is at the extreme of desire for it. This was the extreme of obstinacy, so the meaning of ʿanīd (stubborn) applied.

﴿So he said﴾: meaning, immediately after what his wicked nature led him to in imposing greatness in this manner, because he saw it as beneficial to them in the worldly life and did not reflect on its consequence from the side of God, and that He, glorified is He, does not guide the plot of the treacherous, and the aim of liars does not succeed, and similar things they had tested in their worldly life. How then did he raise his view to the matter of the Hereafter? He emphasized his speech because of what he knew of the denial of the one who would hear him, so he said: ﴿Indeed﴾, meaning: ﴿this is not﴾, meaning [what] Muhammad (ﷺ) brought, ﴿except sorcery﴾, meaning matters of imagination with no realities behind them, and because of their subtlety, their causes are hidden.

Since it was known to them that Muhammad (ﷺ) had never been bewitched and did not know sorcery, whoever claimed that would be known to be a liar with the least reflection, after the command according to his capacity. So he said: ﴿it is related﴾, meaning that by its nature the listener transmits it from another. So, because of the strength of its sorcery and its excess in its field, it separates, by mere transmission, between a man and his wife, and between a man and his father and his son, and so on among the other wonders that arise from it.

Since the listener could think that the speech is transmitted from God, which would make him desire it, He said, without a conjunction, as an explanation of the first statement and an emphasis upon it (the conjunction being omitted because the second clause is a restatement of the first). He presented it in the form of emphasis through restriction (*ḥaṣr*), since He knew that everyone with insight would deny His speech: ﴿Indeed (*in*), i.e., this is not,﴾ meaning the Qur'an, ﴿but the word of a human being.﴾ That is, there is nothing in it from God, so no one should be deceived by it or give it any attention. He praised it through this dispraise after all this reflection, because He established that it is beyond the ability of most people to match, just as they are unable to match magic. So it was silent for a time and then spoke after a while. In some respects, it resembles what one of them said:

*If it were said, "How much is five and five?" he would spend the day and night counting and calculating.*

*He says, "A baffling matter, its wonder,"* and "Indeed, I am more amazed at my own matter than at it."

*Until his hands became numb and his eyes went blind from what he was writing and drawing.*

*He came upon a height and said, "Look!" and nearly swooned and died from joy.*

*"Five and five: six, or seven,"* are two opinions that al-Khalil and Tha'lab both stated.

And so, every truth whose extreme detractor is found: his dispraise does not cease to convey a praise of it, which refutes his own speech. But where are the critics, those counted among the rare individuals among the servants? This speech is applicable to the general case of everyone whom He, glorified is He, created in this manner, in deviating from the truth because of the leadership God has favoured him with, since the people of greatness in this world are, for the most part, those who stand against the truth and who act arrogantly toward its people, as is mentioned here. This does not contradict what they have said: that it was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughira al-Makhzumi. Rather, this is part of the inimitability of God's speech, that a verse be revealed concerning one person, clarifying his condition with the utmost clarity, while that clarification also encompasses others.

They said: al-Walid had ten sons, each of whom was the chief of a tribe, and they had slaves who travelled on their trade and carried out their needs, so they did not require them to leave the city for trade or anything else. Three of them became Muslims: al-Walid ibn al-Walid, Khalid, and Hisham. It was also said that when the first part of Surah Ghafir, up to His saying ﴿the final return﴾ [Ghafir 40:3], or the beginning of Fussilat, was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ, the Prophet ﷺ recited it in the mosque while al-Walid was listening. So he repeated the recitation. Then al-Walid left and came to the assembly of his people, the Banu Makhzum, and said: "By God, I have just heard from Muhammad ﷺ words that are neither the words of humans nor the words of jinn. Indeed, it has sweetness, and indeed it has a brilliance upon it. Its upper part bears fruit, and its lower part is luxuriant, and it rises high and nothing rises above it." Then he departed.

Quraysh said: "By God, al-Walid has turned to Islam! By God, all of Quraysh will turn!" Al-Walid was called "the basil of Quraysh." Then his nephew Abu Jahl said: "I will take care of him for you." So he sat beside al-Walid, looking grieved. Al-Walid said: "What is it, nephew, that I see you grieved?" He said: "What would prevent me, when Quraysh gathers money for you to help you in your old age and claims that you have turned to Islam, so that you may go to the son of Abu Kabsha and the son of Abu Quhafa to obtain some of their food?" Al-Walid became angry and said: "Does Quraysh not know that I am among the most wealthy of them in property and children? Has Muhammad and his companions ever been satisfied with food, so that they would have any surplus?" Then he got up with Abu Jahl and came to the assembly of his people, and they debated among themselves what they should say about the Qur'an. They said to him: "What do you say about this which Muhammad has brought?" He said: "Say it, and I will hear it for you." They said: "Poetry." He said: "It is not poetry. We know all kinds of poetry." In another narration: "Have you seen him attempting poetry?" They said: "Soothsaying." He said: "It is not soothsaying. Have you seen him foretelling?" Then they enumerated the kinds of slander with which they had attacked the Qur'an, and he rejected them, and established the proof for rejecting them. He said: "Do not say any of that, but I know that it is a lie." They said: "Then you say something, and give us an opinion on which we can agree." He said: "The closest of these to it is magic. It separates a man from his father, a man from his wife, and his clan." So they dispersed on that basis. This statement of his was the cause of his destruction, and it turned out as one of them said:

*Guard your tongue, O man, lest it bite you, for it is a serpent.*

*How many in the graveyards are slain by their tongues, whom the brave feared to meet.*

Then, when the explanation of his obstinacy had ended, and there arose an eagerness for the detailing of his recompense in his return (to Allah), He said, clarifying some of what his being burdened with the ascent had implied: ﴿I will cast him into Saqar﴾, meaning, by a threat that cannot be avoided, soon. ﴿Saqar﴾, that is, the fiery abyss which does to the brains, from the intensity of its heat, what is beyond description. So He will cast him into it, and make him endure its hardships, its heat, and his brain will be melted by it, and his mind and all its essence will be made to flow out by its fierce heat, as a recompense for his thinking, this which he measured, imagined and formed by turning it over in the layers of his brain, so that it would burn the livers of the friends of Allah and His chosen ones.

When he had established this punishment for him, He magnified and terrified it by saying: ﴿And what will make you know what Saqar is?﴾ That is, what will inform you, even if you strive in inquiry, [of] what Saqar is? He means that the knowledge of this lies beyond the capacity of humankind, and no one among them can reach it except through God's informing him, because it is too great for any human being to comprehend.

Having established this greatness for it, He increased it in grandeur by describing its action rather than explaining its nature. So He said: ﴿It leaves nothing﴾, meaning this Saqar does not leave anything cast into it in the state of remaining as it was, ﴿nor does it spare﴾, meaning it does not leave it in any state, even the worst of states, let alone what is less than that. Rather, it is constantly destroying everything it has been permitted to destroy, and altering the conditions of those whom it has been permitted to punish, yet it has not been permitted to annihilate them completely. For everything there is a respite and a weariness short of that.

Since a person's condition changing to something lesser than what he is, a distressing affliction for him, when that happens it changes his color, because the outward is the sign of the inward, Allah the Exalted said, indicating the intensity of its action in that: ﴿Scorching⦆... 

Let me give the full translation carefully:

When the change of a person's state to something lower than what he is in, a distressing affliction for him, occurs, it alters his complexion, because the apparent is the sign of the inner. Allah the Exalted said, indicating the severity of its effect in that: ﴿Scorching﴾, meaning intensely altering by blackness, blueness, glaring and agitation [and making thirsty and the like] of the corruption, due to its intense heat. The Arabs say: "The fire scorched the thing" (lāḥat al-nār al-shay'), when it burns it and blackens it. ﴿To the human being﴾, meaning to people or to their skins, plural of basharah (bashara), and the plural of al-bashar is abshār.

[(p-٦١)] Upon it, i.e., upon the Fire in general, as indicated by what follows concerning the guardians. ﴿Nineteen﴾, i.e., nineteen angels. For the category of believers, which is the highest, there is one angel, and for the remaining six categories there are eighteen, three for each category. This is because one angel is supported by a second, and the two of them are strengthened by a third. Therefore, and Allah knows best, they were three. Or, because disbelief is directed against Allah, His books, and His Messenger ﷺ, there was for each act of denial in each of the six categories of the Fire one angel or one class of angels. According to the first view, that they are individual persons, most of the exegetes (mufassirun) hold this position. It has already been established that they are harsh and severe, each one of them sufficient to deal with all the inhabitants of the earth, just as one angel was assigned to seize all the souls. It has come in reports that their eyes are like flashing lightning, their fangs are like the horns (ṣayāṣī), the flame of the Fire issues from their mouths, and the distance between the shoulders of one of them is a year's journey. Mercy has been removed from them. One of them can push seventy thousand and throw them wherever he wishes into Hell. ʿAmr ibn Dinar said: one of them, with a single push, pushes more than Rabiʿah and Mudar (two large tribes). It has also been said: this number corresponds to the faculties present in the human being by which his constitution is maintained, namely the five outward senses: hearing, sight, smell, taste, and touch; the five inward faculties: the imaginative (mutakhayyilah), the estimative (wahimah), the cogitative (mufakkirah), the retentive (hafizah), and the memory (dhakirah); the two powers of appetite (shahwah) and anger (ghadab); and the seven natural faculties: the retentive (masikah), the digestive (hadimah), the attractive (jadhibah), the expulsive (dafiʿah), the nutritive (ghadhiyah), the growth (namiyah), and the generative (muwallidah). It has also been said: this number was chosen because nine is the end of the units, and ten is the beginning of the tens; their sum therefore gathers the largest of the few and the smallest of the many, so it became the most comprehensive of numbers, indicating that its guardians are the most comprehensive of hosts. It is related from Ibn Masʿud (may Allah be pleased with him) that reciting the basmalah (the formula "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate") protects one from the guardians of the Fire, for it has nineteen letters, and each letter belongs to one of the angels among them. [(p-٦٢)]

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 74, verse 31:

Since this number does not distinguish the things counted, and the wisdom in specifying this count is not apparent, and since this number is one that the one seeking to be obstinate considers small, so he increases in disbelief, [the Exalted said], explaining this: ﴿And We have not made﴾, meaning, by the greatness We possess, even if the aspect of that greatness is hidden from one whose heart is blind, ﴿the keepers of the Fire﴾, meaning its guardians, ﴿but angels﴾, meaning they are not of the kind of those who are punished, so that they would feel pity for them, and the punished could not endure their attempts, or find relief in them, while they are the strongest of creation. Their mention has been repeated for you, and you know their attributes, and that they are not like humans. Rather, one of them shouts a single cry and destroys an entire city, as happened to Thamud. So how much more so when each of these guardians has a chief under his command, with troops that none can count except Allah, the Exalted. ﴿And We have not made﴾, given the greatness We possess, ﴿their number﴾, meaning, mentioned and limited to what We have mentioned, ﴿except as a trial﴾, meaning a state that mixes in, inclines and confounds ﴿for those who disbelieve﴾, meaning those who brought about this description, even at the lowest level, for they consider it small, mock it, and are obstinate in various kinds of obstinacy, to the extent that one of the dullards of Quraysh, who was Abu Jahl, (p-63) said: "May your mothers be bereaved! Does the son of Abu Kabsha say such-and-such, while you are his strongest opponents? Can not every ten of you overpower one man of them?" Abu al-Ashadd ibn Usayd ibn Kilda al-Jumahi, who was very strong in seizing, said: "I will suffice you against seventeen; you suffice me against two." All of this is by way of mockery, for they deny the Resurrection, of which this is one of the signs. It was known among the People of the Book that this was their number, and that when the Arabs heard this number, it would be a cause of doubt for most of them and an occasion for obstinacy. Therefore, He linked to the trial, or to "We have made," His saying: ﴿so that those who were given the Book may be certain﴾, meaning certainty comes into being in a complete manner, as if it were with the utmost desire. ﴿Those who were given the Book﴾: the verb is in the passive form, because the mere giving is sufficient for this, without need to specify the Giver, although it is well known that He is Allah. Al-Baghawi said: it is written in the Torah and the Gospel that they are nineteen.

﴿And that those who believe may increase in faith﴾, meaning they bring about this truth, even at the lowest level, in addition to the faith they already have, ﴿in faith﴾, by affirming what they did not know the wisdom of. This is especially so given the temptation of others by it and the abundance of their talk about it, for faith in such a matter is greater.

When He established for each of the ignorant and the knowledgeable what He established, He confirmed it by negating its opposite, explaining the trial, and said: ﴿And those who were given the Book will not doubt﴾, meaning they will not have a doubt arising from deliberate intent and acquisition, ﴿because of what they have of knowledge that agrees with this.﴾ Ibn Burjan said: Jabir ibn Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with both of them, narrated that "a group of the People of the Book came to him in a matter that was lengthy, and in it they asked him about the guardians of Hell. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gestured with his hand thus and thus, once ten and once nine. They said: May Allah bless you, O Abu al-Qasim. Then he asked them: What are the guardians of Paradise? They fell silent out of awe, then said: A loaf of bread, O Abu al-Qasim. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: The loaf is of fine flour." ﴿And the believers﴾, meaning those in whom faith is firmly established will not doubt, because of the proofs they have seen which have placed them in the like of the light of day. ﴿And that those in whose hearts is a disease﴾, meaning, in whose hearts there is firmly settled doubt or hypocrisy, even if slight, ﴿may say﴾. The revelation of this surah before the existence of the hypocrites is one of the signs of prophethood. It is not denied that Allah, the Exalted, makes some matters a cause for the benefit of some people and the corruption of others, because He is not questioned about what He does. Moreover, a cause may itself be intended for one thing as a primary intent, and then something else is ordered upon it, whose intent is secondary. You say: "I left the town to oppose the majority and to fear evil," and the purpose is not tied to it. ﴿And the disbelievers﴾, meaning those firmly rooted in disbelief, who are resolute in denial, who openly declare it, and who conceal what the evidences indicate of the truth, ﴿say: What﴾, meaning what thing, ﴿did Allah intend﴾, meaning the King who possesses all greatness, ﴿by this﴾, meaning this small number in comparison with His greatness, ﴿as an example﴾, meaning, in that by it they have become astonished with the astonishment of one who is amazed by a parable, or that this is an indication that its apparent meaning is not what is intended, but rather (p-65) it is a parable for something they did not understand, and they understood that there is a contradiction between possessing greatness and this number, out of obstinacy. They did not know that a small number may be greater in its strength than a large number, and may be more indicative of the possession of greatness.

Since the implied meaning is: He intended by this to lead astray whoever goes astray, while He does not care, and to guide whoever is guided, while He does not care, it is as if it were said: Does He do the like of this in other than this? So He answered: ﴿Thus﴾, meaning like this mentioned matter of misguidance and guidance, ﴿Allah leads astray﴾, meaning He who possesses the assemblies of greatness and the bonds of might, ﴿whom He wills﴾, by whatever speech He wills, ﴿and guides﴾, by His perfect power, ﴿whom He wills﴾, by that same speech or by something else. This is among the wisdoms of making the guardians nineteen and informing about them with that count, for presenting rulings in a manner of obscurity is among the greatest things that destroy or make happy. The one whose nature is deviant seeks their causes with obstinate investigation, and when they are hidden from him, he decides that those rulings are false or doubts them, and perhaps refuses to submit. This is the cause of Iblis's disbelief. But the one of sound temperament [investigates] along with submission. If the matter becomes clear to him, he increases in submission; otherwise he says: "We believe in it; all of it is from our Lord," and he is in the utmost degree of complete submission to what (p-66) knows its secret. May Allah grant us submission to His command, and help us to remember and thank Him.

Since this matter may give the impression of the small number of His hosts, the Exalted, He followed it with what removes that: ﴿And none knows the hosts of your Lord﴾, meaning, while the state is that none knows, ﴿your Lord﴾, meaning the One who is good to you with all kinds of goodness, who manages your affair with the utmost perfection, by making the Fire and its guardians and placing them at this number and other than that, ﴿except He﴾, meaning the greatest King, encompassing all attributes of perfection. So, if He wished to make the guardians more than that, He could. It has been narrated that "seventy thousand angels enter the Bayt al-Ma'mur (the frequented house in the heavens) every day, and they do not return to it in another turn." It has also been reported in a report: "The earth in the heaven is like a ring thrown in a desert, and every heaven in relation to the one above it is likewise." And it has been reported in a hadith: "The heaven groaned, and it has the right to groan. There is not a place of a foot in it except that there is an angel standing in prayer."

This number was specified for wisdoms that none knows except Him, and for whoever He wills of His servants to be informed of it, although sufficiency occurs without that. There was among the angels one who uprooted the cities of the people of Lot, which were seven, and lifted them up to the height of the sky. Everything in the human being of substances (p-67) and accidents is among Allah's hosts; if something of his own self were set against him, it would destroy him: if a still vein moved, or a moving one stilled, or a hollow were blocked, or a blocked one became hollow, he would perish.

Since He mentioned some of the secrets of conveying reports about these matters, which are obscure, and since that is among the mercies to the servants, so that He opens for them a door to submission to what is obscure, by reminding them of the matter of their Sovereign. Because the weak person cannot, in walking according to the law of wisdom, do anything but submit to the Almighty; otherwise he would destroy himself and harm no one else. He specified the matter of the Fire in reminding, as an emphasis for informing, as a reminder of a blessing, because of the crookedness of natures that most of the addressees have, which calls for rejection and denial, and which calls for speech to be given in the manner of emphasis. So He said: ﴿And it is not﴾, meaning the Fire, which is among the greatest of His hosts, glory be to Him and exalted, ﴿except a reminder to mankind﴾, meaning a great reminder for everyone who is of human skin, for his body is the most receptive of things to be affected by it, because of what they know of it in their worldly life. Otherwise, He, glory be to Him and exalted, is able to create what is more severe than it, greater, and more painful, of which creation has no knowledge.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 74, verse 32:

When the restriction of its (Hell's) matter to being a reminder might perhaps give the impression of a deficiency in its affair, which would cause some of the obstinate ones to doubt its magnitude and to think that it has no reality and no punishment in it, He said, deterring from that and alerting to readiness and caution, with the word of deterrence (p-68) and alerting: ﴿Nay﴾, that is, beware of doubting its terrors, its great affair, its conditions and its frights, because the matter is more all-encompassing and greater than what comes to mind, so let the hearer be restrained and let him desist.

When He had restricted its affair to being a reminder and negated that one might suppose any deficiency in it with respect to that for which it was made, He added emphasis to the speech, as an indication of the stubbornness and crookedness that most of the addressees possess, to awaken them from the heedlessness they are in, to soften the blame and density they have, and to alert them to striving to correct their souls by means of the remedies that He, glorified is He, guides them to use for curing the diseases of the hearts. He increased the matter in emphasis, so He swore an oath upon that by that which is a reminder for mankind, and with which the darkness of the night does not remain, just as the light of the Qur'an does not leave with it the darkness of ignorance for whoever applies the eye of his reflection and casts aside the portions of his own self. So He said: ﴿By the moon﴾ [that is, which] is the sign of the night, guiding whoever has gone astray by its darkness.

"And by the night when it turns back" — that is, when it passes on and withdraws, returning from the direction it came, so that its darkness is uncovered; with its uncovering, ignorance departs, and with its withdrawal, doubts and suspicions are dispelled.

﴿By the dawn when it brightens.﴾ Its light came forth, so knowledge became manifest through its arrival, and guidance was attained through its coming. Or [the verb] *dabara*, in the sense of *aqbala* ("came forward"). Qutrub said: The Arabs say, *dabarani fulan*, meaning, "So-and-so came up behind me."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 74, verse 35:

When He had sworn to what He had reported of her mention, and emphasized it because of their great denial of her calamities, He began to magnify her and to warn of her, as an emphasis on the warning in light of the denial that preceded. So He said: ﴿Indeed, it﴾, that is, the Fire, which is Saqar, is one of its levels (darakat, "the deep tiers" of Hell), and He increased the emphasis in accordance with the increase in their mockery, so He said: ﴿is one of the greatest (al-kubar)﴾, that is, among the calamities and great matters. It is the plural of kabira and kubra, and it is a metaphor (kinaya) for the intensity of its terror, as one says: "He is one of the men," meaning he has no equal. Or the intended meaning is that it is one of seven, being the utmost in greatness, that is, the levels of the Fire, which are Jahannam, then Laza, then al-Hutama, then al-Sa'ir, then Saqar, then al-Jahim, then al-Hawiyah. It is one of them in the greatness of its regions and the severity of its pain and harm, while it is

﴿Nadhīran﴾ (a warner): a great warning, or a warning in terms of its warning-ness, or an effective, far-reaching warning. It is *fa'īl* (a noun pattern in Arabic grammar) in the sense of the *maṣdar* (verbal noun), like ﴿So how was My rejection?﴾ [al-Mulk: 18], meaning My rejection (*inkārī*). He expressed it with His saying ﴿to mankind﴾ because of what preceded, namely the indication that the ordinary human body is quick to accept being affected, especially by fire.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 74, verse 37:

Since advancing (al-taqaddum) is loved by people, especially the Arabs, and lagging behind (al-ta'akhkhur) is disliked, and since Glorified and Exalted is He had created in man a power and a will by which he does what God has decreed for him, while concealing from him knowledge of the outcome, so that the act is attributed to him even though it is in fact by God's creation, He said, urging them toward good and keeping them away from evil, in a resumptive clause (musta'nafan) or in a substitution (mubdilan), as an answer to one who says: "What might we do?" or "Will warning benefit?" And He had already said that He is the Guide and the Misleader: ﴿God misleads whom He wills and guides whom He wills﴾ [wa-yahdi man yasha' -]: ﴿for whoever among you wills﴾, that is, by His will. He stated the intended meaning explicitly so that the one who seeks to quibble among them would not say, "The intent is other than us," so He said: ﴿among you﴾, that is, O you obstinate ones, ﴿to advance﴾, that is, toward the good deeds, ﴿or to lag behind﴾, that is, from them, and so he reaches the anger of God Most High and the Fire, which is the effect of His anger, which He made what is near us of painful heat and destructive cold to be an effect proceeding from its essence, as a reminder to us and as mercy toward us. The object has been omitted because its use is frequent, to the point that it is understood even when it is not mentioned. The rendering of this is: for whoever wills to advance, the advancing by what he has of capacity and choice in the outward sense, and for whoever wills to lag behind, the lagging behind. ﴿To advance﴾ (an yataqaddama) is the subject (mubtada'), and it is an example like "for whoever performs ablution, that he should pray" (li-man yatawaddha'u an yusalliya). It is also permissible for the clause to be a substitution (badal) for "for mankind" (li-l-bashar), by way of the shift from the third person to the second person (iltifat), so that each person addressed becomes as though he himself were the primary intended party, so that he reflects on the meaning within himself, finds it true, and then reflects further and finds no obstacle to extending it to others among all mankind. In this case, "an" and the verb are the object (maf'ul) of "shā'a" (wills).

Since advancing and delaying are by deeds, and most of man's deeds are evil because of the deficiency he was created with, he said, explaining what he advances and what he delays: ﴿Every soul﴾, i.e., male or female, in general, ﴿for what it has earned﴾, i.e., specifically, not for what another has earned, ﴿is held in pledge﴾, i.e., held as a pledge by its deed. "Rahīnah" is a noun in the sense of "pledge (rahn)," as in the line of the poet al-Hamasi:

After the one who is by the sandy tract, Kuwaykib, is a pledge
for the grave of one with dust and gravel.

"Rahīn," which is an adjective, does not take a feminine form, because fa'īl in the sense of maf'ūl has the same form for masculine and feminine. Had the rhyming endings, which they use to refer to saj' out of courtesy, been observed in the Qur'an in any way, it would have said "rahīn," for the sake of the rhyme with yamīn. But no consideration is given to this apart from meaning. It is also permissible that the ta' (in rahīnah) is for emphasis, in the sense of "bound with a strong binding, held in a great confinement, so he is in the Fire," and thus the basis is made the earned deed that is bound.

Since a pledge (rahn) is sometimes redeemed and sometimes forfeited, and most of creation is destroyed, he made "rahina" mean "destroyed" (halikah). Then he excepted the praised ones, saying: ﴿Except the companions of the right hand﴾, that is, those whose description has already preceded, who are the ones who withdrew to Allah, complied with His commands, and refrained from His prohibitions. Indeed, they are not held in pledge for their deeds; rather, Allah shows them mercy, accepts their good deeds, and overlooks their misdeeds.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 74, verse 40:

When He had removed them from the ruling of pledged-ness (al-irtihan), which he applied to destruction because it is its cause, he resumed explaining their condition, saying: ﴿In gardens﴾, that is, orchards of the utmost greatness, because they had released themselves and freed their necks, so they were not held in pledge. The verse is of the type called ihtibak (mutual omission): he first affirmed pledged-ness as an indication of the omission of its opposite second, and second affirmed the garden as an indication of the omission of its opposite first.

And since asking about the state of others clearly indicates ease and freedom from everything that burdens the soul, he expressed their ease through the most sublime admonition and the most gentle warning in His words: ﴿they will ask one another﴾, that is, among themselves, some of them asking others.
﴿About the criminals﴾, i.e., the circumstances of those who are deeply rooted in severing what Allah has commanded to be joined.

The commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 74, verse 42:

When the Day of Resurrection reaches the utmost of severity, and each person is preoccupied with himself, so that he has no knowledge of the details of what happens to others, and when the friends of God enter the abode of His honour, they wish to know what He has done with their enemies, may He be exalted. So they ask one another about their condition, and some of them say to others: "We have no knowledge of them." Then God (exalted is He) unveils them to them, until they see them in the Fire, which is being kindled with them, so that God may delight their eyes with their punishment, as an increase in their bliss and reward. This was already mentioned in al-Saffat at His saying ﴿One of them will say: Indeed, I had a companion﴾ [al-Saffat: 51]. The flow of the discourse indicates all of this. He, may He be exalted, pointed us to it by His saying, relating what their friends say to them as rebuke, reproach, mockery and reproof, confirming His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿So today those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 34], and so that the relating of this may be an admonition to the listeners and a reminder to those who remember: ﴿What﴾ is open to the meaning of rebuke and of astonishment. ﴿Salakakum﴾ means: "He caused you to enter," O guilty ones, an entry that is in the utmost narrowness, until it is as if you were the thread passing through the hole, ﴿into Saqar﴾. So this address conveys that, when they asked, they denied knowledge of themselves. It is known that the denial of knowledge is because they were occupied with themselves, and that they were occupied only because that day is full of great preoccupations, despite their being among the people of felicity. It is also known that if knowledge of the condition of the people of Paradise was impossible for them, while they did not intend to seek intercession on their behalf, then no way remained to know that except by asking them about themselves, since it is not thought that seeking intercession would be the aim, except by questioning them about themselves, so that they address them with this, and thus they learn their state, so that they may increase in joy and gladness at what God has saved them from the likes of their condition, and may abound in praise of God, may He be exalted, for having granted them success in it. And so that this may be an admonition for us through our hearing of it. Thus God related that when they asked them,

﴿They said﴾, mentioning the reason for their entry into the Fire: they corrupted their practical capacity in glorifying God's command. It is a summary (fadhlaka) of all the principal matters of the surah that preceded, the gist of which is that they were not adorned with two virtues and were not free of two vices. This identifies them as people addressed with the branches (furu') of the Sharia (the detailed legal rulings). In beginning with practice there is an alert that the rational person must hasten to what the Truthful One (al-Sadiq) commands him, since that practice confirms sound belief (husn al-i'tiqad). Hastening to engage in practice is easier than hastening to engage in knowledge, because practice has a form (surah) and a reality (haqiqah). Mere representation (taswir) is easier than verification (tahqiq), and whoever forms an image of something is closer to realizing it than one who has not formed it, so he is more worthy of realizing it than one who has not undertaken its representation. Thus there is in this an exhortation to race toward righteous deeds even if the intention is not pure, and a notice that whoever persists in abandoning deeds is led by that to be stripped of sound belief and plunged into misguidance.

﴿We were not﴾: they dropped the nun, indicating the constriction they are in that prevents them from speaking even a letter that could be dispensed with, and indicating that they had no kind of good disposition that would urge them to be counted among the righteous. This points to the magnitude of the overwhelming calamities occupying them, the opposite of the leisure of the people of Paradise, which moves them to ask about the conditions of others. This also alerts to the virtue of knowledge: ﴿of those who prayed﴾ [i.e., prayer that is counted valid] (p-75). This is an alert that firmness of foot in prayer prevents one from a state like theirs, and that they are punished for the branches of the Sharia even though those branches would not be valid from them; so if they had performed them before faith, they would not have been counted. It also indicates that prayer is the greatest of the deeds, and that reckoning begins with it before other deeds.

When they denied the connection with the Creator, they followed it with corrupting the practical faculty by severing their connection with creatures, through abandoning compassion for the creation of God [so they said]: ﴿We were not﴾ (dropping the nun here as well) because of the state of misery they were in, and to negate even the slightest part of good disposition: ﴿feeding the needy﴾, that is, on account of his neediness. Here they negated the existence of feeding him, for if they happened to feed him, it was for some reason other than his neediness. As for prayer, they do perform it [for God], in their own claim, but [since] it was not in the manner they were commanded, it was not accepted, and so they were not among the firmly rooted in describing it.

When He stripped them of adorning themselves with the garments of the friends of God, He established for them adorning themselves with the garments of the wretched, by corrupting the faculty of speech, joining speech to action. So they said: ﴿And we used to﴾, that is, by reason of the evil with which He created us, ﴿plunge﴾, that is, we bring into being speech that is out of its places, and we have no knowledge of it, bringing into being the walking of one who wades into deep water [from the one plunging into deep water-] (p-76) ﴿along with those who plunge﴾, to the extent that this became for us [a firmly established attribute, so we say of the Qur'an: it is magic, it is poetry, it is soothsaying, and other than this] of the falsehoods. We do not refrain from any of that, nor do we stop at reason, nor do we turn to sound transmission. So let those who hasten to speak on every kind of knowledge they are asked about, without first establishing their own rank [from -] here, take heed.

When persistence in falsehood leads inevitably to a dominance of mockery and derision, and that dominance in turn necessarily brings about the corruption of the faculty of knowledge through believing falsehood and denying truth, they said, explaining their preference for [remaining in] eternity: ﴿And we used to deny the Day of Judgment﴾, meaning, to such a degree that this became a fixed attribute of ours.

Since the implied meaning is: "and our denial persisted, because it had become for us established attributes," they built upon it their saying: ﴿until there came to us﴾, that is, definitively, ﴿the certainty﴾, that is, by death, or by its preliminaries which cut us off from [dār -] action, so faith in the unseen collapsed.

So when they confessed against themselves to what brought upon them the everlasting punishment, and they were among those whose temperament had become corrupt, so that their cure was impossible, its consequence was His saying: ﴿So the intercession of the intercessors will not benefit them﴾, that is, while they are characterized by these attributes, and this state is a constant condition for them always, even if the intercessors were to intercede for them.

Since this report of the blessings of the Bestower and the punishment of the one punished was bound to lead to remembrance, al-Biqa'i says that it causes a rebuke directed at them, so He says: ﴿So what is wrong with them﴾, i.e., what could be the case with them, ﴿that they turn away from the reminder﴾, i.e., from the great reminder, specifically the Qur'an in particular and anything else in general, ﴿turning away﴾, and [they are] inclined only toward falsehood. That is among the most astonishing of wonders, because when a person is warned of something, human nature makes him guard against it with the utmost caution, as when a traveler is warned of a beast of prey on his path, so he exerts his effort to swerve away from it and to beware of it, even if the one giving the warning is lying. How then do they turn away from this greatest thing to be feared, when the one informing is the most truthful of the truthful? Their turning away here is evidence of the disorder of their minds and the confusion of their understanding. What made this more astonishing still was the intensity of their aversion, until

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 74, verse 50:

﴿As if they﴾ in their aversion from the reminder, out of extreme fleeing and hastening in flight, ﴿were donkeys﴾, that is, of the wild asses, which are among the most skittish of creatures. For this reason, most of the Arabs' comparisons describing camels' swiftness of travel were to wild asses in their running when they came to water and sensed something there that alarmed them. In likening the disbelievers to donkeys, especially in this state, there is clear blame and evident disparagement of their condition, and a testimony against them of foolishness, scant intellect, and lack of steadiness. ﴿Fleeing﴾, that is, causing flight (p-78) with the utmost eagerness for it, as though they sought it from themselves because it is part of their nature and disposition. This is according to the reading of the majority. Ahl al-Madina and al-Sham, however, read it with a fatha (mustanfiratun as mustanfarah), meaning that something caused them to flee.

Since that would not happen except from a great cause that one longs to know about, he resumed his statement: ﴿They flee from a lion﴾, that is, a lion of great might and overpowering force, so they are caught in the snares of Saqar, or of hunters.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 74, verse 52:

When the answer was decisively given, namely that there is nothing for them in this aversion of theirs, he turned away from it with His saying: ﴿Nay, every one of them wishes﴾ — that is, [upon] their claim and in their assumption — ﴿that he be given﴾ — that is, from the heavens; He built the verb in the passive because what they intend is well known — ﴿scrolls spread out﴾ — that is, many written pages, very numerous, each one of them open, with nothing preventing its being read and taken up — even though he claims perfection in manliness, of the ones turning away. And that is because they said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "We will not follow you until you bring each of us a book from heaven containing: 'From God to so-and-so: follow Muhammad (ﷺ).'"

Since that was merely obstinacy and not that they wanted it in its reality, He said: ﴿Nay﴾, meaning they have no purpose in following in any way whatsoever, neither with this condition nor with any other: ﴿Rather﴾, their true cause for this turning away is that they ﴿do not fear﴾, meaning at no time whatsoever, ﴿the Hereafter﴾.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 74, verse 54:

Since their action was that of one who believes the Qur'an is not a sound admonition deserving to be followed, He said, deterring them from this implication: ﴿Nay!﴾ That is, the matter is certainly not as you claim, that this Qur'an does not deserve to be heeded. Then He resumed His statement, emphasizing it because of what this action contained of their denial: ﴿Indeed, it﴾, that is, the Qur'an, ﴿is a reminder﴾, that is, a place of great admonition which makes it obligatory, with great obligation, to follow it and not to turn away from it in any way. So no one may say, "I am excused, because I did not find a reminder or a guide." For with it is the greatest reminder and the most noble distinguisher.

Since it (the Qur'an) is in the utmost ease and sweetness for everyone who knows it in any respect, and since Allah, glorified is He, has created the faculties and divine decree and has made for the servant choice (ikhtiyar), He said, as a consequence of its being a place for remembrance: ﴿So whoever wills﴾, meaning, to remember it, ﴿remembers it﴾, so it becomes firmly fixed in his breast, he knows its meaning, and he takes on its character. No one [is able] to say that it is hard in its composition, great in its complexity, difficult to understand, requiring in extracting its meanings a great effort and long practice, so that I am excused for stopping before it. Rather, [it] is like the great river Euphrates: whoever wills, scoops from it. This is because it was addressed to an unlettered people who had no practice in any of the sciences, so it was made extremely easy in its wording and its meaning, although it cannot be reached to its bottom, nor can one hope to contend with a single one of its traces, rather, the more a person reflects upon it, the more meanings it increases for him.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 74, verse 56:

Since [this -] may give the impression that the servant has independent power to act, he said, teaching that this is only a metaphor for the ease, sweetness and pleasantness of the Qur'an, which make it beloved to every person of understanding, and alerting to abandoning self-admiration and showing humility, dependence and need upon the Mighty, the Forgiving, in seeking success toward the most upright path: ﴿And they will not remember﴾, that is, [and -] none of you, nor this Qur'an nor anything else, at any time, ﴿unless Allah wills﴾, [that is -] the Greatest King, with whom no one has any command. This is explicit that the servant's action is among what He wills, and whatever arises from it [is only -] by the will of Allah.

* *

Since it has been established that He, glory be to Him, is the Doer of what He wills, and that no one has any action without His will, and since it is known that most of the actions of the servants are of what does not please Him, were it not for His forbearance they would not have been able to do so, and the pardon of one who is able is praiseworthy, He said, explaining that He is worthy of [awe -] and desire: ﴿He is﴾, that is, He alone, ﴿the One worthy of being feared﴾, that is, that His servants should fear Him and beware of His anger with all that their ability reaches, because of His majesty, [and -] greatness and dominion. It is also possible that the pronoun refers to the one who fears Him: ﴿and the One worthy of forgiveness﴾ (p-81), that is, that one should seek His forgiveness of sins, especially when the sinner fears Him, because He possesses beauty and kindness, He is able, and no one else has power; nothing benefits Him and nothing harms Him. He is thus deserving that the place of warning which He commanded at the beginning of the surah be made a place of good news, and that He grant His servants success in magnifying Him and abandoning ar-rijz (idolatry). Glory be to Him, He did likewise with the people of this noble Prophet ﷺ. Ahmad, at-Tirmidhi, an-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, at-Tabarani in al-Awsat, al-Hakim, Abu Ya'la, al-Baghawi and al-Bazzar related from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, that "the Prophet ﷺ recited this verse and then said: Allah says, 'I am worthy that I be feared; so whoever fears that he should associate another with Me, [then -] I am worthy that I forgive him.'" At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Adi and at-Tabarani said: Sahl ibn [Abi -] Hazm al-Qat'i narrated it alone. He returned the end of the surah to its beginning, and its joint joined with what it connects to, by combining good news with warning. It is as if it was said: warn the disobedient, for he is worthy of returning to his acts of obedience, and so He, glory be to Him, is worthy of covering his slips.
